A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 27 pages of v2 and 34 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-classification experiments, repeated-run accuracy measurements, learning curves, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification experiments and adds learning-rate, representation, throughput, and learned-residual diagnostics.

M1.justification: The proposed update in Eqs. (3)–(4), stability constant, feature-wise/global variants, and PyTorch implementations remain unchanged. The new learned-scaling and mixing variants are diagnostic comparators. Algorithm 1 introduces a denominator inconsistency, but the unchanged equation and code do not support interpreting it as an actual method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-1k. The added diagnostics vary models, parameters, or measurements within this coverage; they introduce no new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated diagnostic alternatives: learned per-layer stream scaling in Section 3.5 and a trainable parallel/orthogonal mixing family with linear and orthogonal starts in Appendix E. Their trajectories are reported. The comparator membership in the main classification table remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include a five-value learning-rate sweep, effective-rank/entropy/CKA/feature-variability measurements, matched-condition throughput measurements, and specified initializations for residual-family diagnostics. The main splits, architectures, epoch budgets, and best-five-validation-epoch aggregation remain unchanged. The added minimum-learning-rate row is a disclosure, not evidence of a changed existing setting.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analyses of learning-rate robustness, representation diversity, and competing explanations involving learned scaling and parallel/orthogonal mixing. Existing initialization, LayerNorm, connection-switching, probability, layer-placement, and epsilon studies remain. The no-reset switching scores move to Table 6; their former learning-curve Figure 9 is omitted.

E5.justification: Table 2 now reports five runs throughout, replacing v2's three-run exception for the ViT-S ImageNet linear baseline. New Figure 4 introduces median and interquartile-range reporting. Conversely, the relocated connection-transfer table captions omit their previously explicit five-run counts. The PDFs do not explain which additional runs were performed.

E6.justification: Headline ImageNet results change in Table 2: ViT-B linear/orthogonal accuracy changes from 71.09/75.45 to 73.27/77.05, and ViT-S from 67.42/70.17 to 70.76/72.53. Figure 2's learning curves are replaced, and new learning-rate, representation, throughput, and residual-variant findings are reported. Most existing classification and ablation scores remain unchanged. The reason for the revised ImageNet results is not documented.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds manifold/tangent-space assumptions and an exponential-map approximation. Appendix B.4 revises reasoning about zero projection and zero input, replacing v2's unrelated rationality discussion. Appendix E defines the mixing family mathematically. Existing projection and Jacobian derivations remain; the identity-gradient argument is relocated rather than newly established.

C1.justification: The abstract's claimed ViT-B ImageNet benefit changes from +4.3 to +3.78 percentage points. The conclusion replaces claims of consistently improved generalization, stability, and efficiency with observed generalization improvements and distinct dynamics at modest overhead. The central contribution and image-classification scope remain.

C2.justification: v3 expands the mechanism explanation through linear-path parallel suppression, learned-scaling comparisons, representation spectra, and manifold geometry. Section 4.4 explicitly attributes switching benefits to update geometry rather than optimizer resets using retained experiments. It also adds reasons for restricting global projection to CNNs and identifies long-horizon stability as unresolved.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code/model access link and minimum learning rates in Appendix A. Hardware, training-time disclosures, and PyTorch functions are retained. However, merged Algorithm 1 replaces the correct squared-input denominator with a repeated input-output dot product, contradicting Eq. (3) and Appendix G and reducing implementation clarity.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kornblith et al.'s representation-similarity work for CKA and removes the SGDR and Inception/label-smoothing references. The related-work prose is condensed, while positioning against skip-path modifications, orthogonal training, and orthogonal finetuning remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial rewrites and reorganization affect the introduction, related work, mechanism discussion, connection-transfer analysis, conclusion, and Appendix D. Gradient arguments and width-to-depth explanations move into appendices, transfer regimes gain separate subsections, and a NeurIPS checklist is inserted. Author affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v3 merges two algorithms, expands Table 1 with throughput, adds diagnostic tables and figures, and redraws Figure 2 with relative wall-clock time. Existing stream, parallel-component, and cosine panels are recombined and partly duplicated across Figures 3, 10, and 11. Transfer scores move into the main text, while their earlier curve figure is removed.

improvement.justification: The added learning-rate and throughput evidence strengthens robustness and efficiency assessment, and the access information improves usability. However, v3 introduces a wrong denominator in Algorithm 1 and representation results in Table 4 whose effective ranks do not match exp(H), as defined in Section 4.3. These inconsistencies affect reproducibility and the new mechanistic evidence. The benefits and harms prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
